relationships.subject: Cannabidiol
relationships.evidence_quote: CBD potently inhibits hNav1.7 (IC₅₀ ≈ 1.8 µM), accompanied by a marked hyperpolarizing shift in Vh1/2 (up to − 11.5 mV at 1 µM) (Huang et al. 2023).

relationships.subject: Cannabidiol
relationships.evidence_quote: In DRG neurons were reported that CBD (5 µM) produced a strong reduction in Nav1.8 peak currents (85%), with progressive hyperpolarization of Vh1/2 depending on conditioning pulse duration.

relationships.subject: Cannabigerol
relationships.evidence_quote: Cannabigerol (CBG) inhibited hNav1.7 currents in a voltage- and holding potential–dependent manner (IC50 values between 4.6 and 18.8 µM).

relationships.subject: Cannabigerol
relationships.evidence_quote: In DRG neurons, CBG dose-dependently decreased AP firing, with up to ~ 89% inhibition at 15 µM (Ghovanloo et al. 2022).

relationships.subject: Cannabidiol
relationships.evidence_quote: Combining electrophysiology and cryo-electron microscopy, CBD binds to two distinct sites on the Nav1.7 channel, neither of which directly occludes the pore, instead, CBD inhibits the channel allosterically (Fig. 3a) (Huang et al. 2023).

key_findings: Systematic review of 7 studies: CBD inhibits Nav1.3, 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8 with low micromolar IC50, stabilizes inactivated states and reduces AP firing.
Other phytocannabinoids (CBG, CBN, CBGA, CBDVA) also inhibit Nav channels with variable potency.
